incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P-3245 triggered — elevated 95th percentile latency for streaming responses in us-west-2 (inference-rt cluster). Auto-alert at 02:13 UTC. On-call: erica

erica: grabbing it. Paging infra/runtime and support. Samir, Nate, Maya, please join.

samir: I'm seeing request_queue_length spike on inference-rt-44 and rt-46. GPU util high, tail lat > 1200ms for streaming endpoints. Non-streamed generation endpoints look much healthier (p95 ~ 300ms).

nate: Confirmed. KV cache churn and frequent short-lived SSE sessions. Lots of tiny streams causing backend pressure.

maya: If streams are the problem, can we temporarily switch streaming endpoints to return final responses (non-stream) to reduce connection overhead?

erica: Proposed live mitigation: 1) flip global runtime toggle to disable push/SSE streaming for hosted API (10–30m trial) 2) temporarily shift quota allotments from streaming to non-stream tokens 3) apply conservative rate-limit for new streaming session creations. Need quick ack.

leah: Support impact: affected customers will receive full responses instead of streaming frames. Some low-latency interactive clients may see slightly higher time-to-first-byte, but overall tail latency should improve. If we go >30m we'll post an update on status.redwood.ai.

samir: How to flip: control-plane toggle. Command below (admin):

```
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/toggles" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"key":"streaming_push_enabled","value":false,"scope":"global"}'
```

erica: I'm going to apply the toggle now. Nate, watch tail p50/p95, queue length, and error rates. Maya, prepare the fallback mapping so /v1/chat/stream -> /v1/chat/generate (non-stream) for SDKs.

nate: Toggle applied. Metrics: within 90s p95 dropped from ~1200ms to ~350ms, queue length decreased ~70%. GPU util stable at ~85%. Error rate unchanged. Mitigation looks effective.

support-bot: Noted — drafting customer update. Will include expected behavior and list of endpoints.

maya: Rolling the mapping as a canary (10%) to avoid sudden client breaks, will ramp to 100% in 2 minutes if stable.

samir: Heads-up: some SDKs still expect SSE; they'll hit client-side timeouts. Suggest we add response header for telemetry and bump client timeout recommendations to 60s during the window. Also add X-Stream-Fallback header.

erica: Good call. Nate, inject header at edge:

```
edgectl set-response-header --name "X-Stream-Fallback" --value "true" --route "/v1/chat/stream"
```

nate: Header deployed. Telemetry event streaming_disabled=true emitted to logs and alerting.

leah: Support note ready: short message for orgs with streaming integrations. Will reference status page and describe what to expect: final payloads, possible client reconnects, timeframe.

erica: Assign follow-ups: samir -> open INF ticket for kernel/kv tuning; maya -> SDK compatibility runbook for graceful fallback; leah -> status + customer comm; nate -> update dashboards and alarms. Leave streaming disabled until we have 30m of stable p95 < 500ms.

samir: Opening INF-987 with current logs and a summary of observed KV eviction patterns.

erica: On-call rotation reminder: handoff in ~45m to nate then maya. Keep this channel open and do not close until streaming is fully re-enabled and postmortem is drafted.

support-bot: Incident P-3245 created and linked to JIRA INF-987.

erica: Thanks. We'll monitor and re-enable carefully.

nate: Running a controlled re-enable test at +28m: streaming_enable=true to 10% throttle. Observed p95 blip to ~680ms, then back to ~420ms. Holding at 10% to check for regressions.

maya: After 40m of stable metrics, plan to ramp to 50% then 100% over 5m. SDK timeouts reduced once clients see final payloads instead of hanging on incomplete streams.

samir: Postmortem action items: tune prefix/KV cache eviction thresholds for short sequences, improve kernel selection heuristics for many small streams, add a graceful-degrade flag in SDKs so clients can switch modes automatically.

erica: Incident summary: streaming push responses disabled for ~37 minutes; mitigation reduced request queueing and brought p95 back into SLO. Customer-facing effect: final non-streaming responses instead of SSE frames. Follow-up: full postmortem, infra tuning, SDK runbook, and an automated safe-toggle playbook to avoid manual pushes next time. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident P-3245 resolved. Duration: 00:37:10. Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/P-3245, https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-987
